"Zainab, my neighbour swears there's a healer who cures it in a week," Aditi said. "He says stop the hospital medicine."
Zainab shook her head. "No. I've been up at dawn every day for my prayers, and honestly it holds me together. When I'm on that mat, the fear goes quiet."
"So you'd rather stay with the hospital?"
"I'd stay with both. I pray, and I go to my Thursday treatment. Nobody gets to swap one for the other."
"What would you like from me?"
"Sit with me on Thursday. And if my aunts bring a blessed thread, I'll wear it. I'll just also take my medicine."
Aditi laughed softly. "Deal."

qa.q: What did the neighbour's healer say Zainab should stop?
qa.a: The healer said to stop the hospital medicine.

qa.q: Why does Zainab say prayer "holds me together"?
qa.a: On the prayer mat her fear goes quiet, so prayer gives her steadiness and comfort.

qa.q: How can Zainab combine faith and treatment?
qa.a: Keep the dawn prayers and accept blessings from family, while continuing the Thursday treatment and her medicine.

qa.q: How might Aditi see the healer's promise of a cure in a week?
qa.a: Aditi probably worries that it could replace real treatment, which is why Aditi raised it and then asked how to help.

grounding: Prayer and ritual bring solace in illness; Zainab lets faith hold her and also follows treatment, refusing a miracle promise that replaces medicine.

passage:
"You've been going to the church prayer group every evening since the diagnosis," Thomas said, handing his brother a cup of tea. "Is it helping?"

"More than anything," Mohit said. "When they pray for me, I stop shaking. I sleep."

"Good. Then keep going."

Mohit looked at the tea. "There's a man who came last week. A healer. He says if I have enough faith, I can stop the chemotherapy. He says the medicines show doubt."

Thomas set his own cup down. "What does Father Joseph say?"

"He says pray and take the medicine. God works through doctors too."

"And what do you think?"

Mohit was quiet a long time. "I think I'm scared of the chemo. And the healer's offer sounds easier."

"It sounds easier," Thomas said gently. "It isn't safer. Keep the prayers. Keep the chemo. Both."

Mohit nodded slowly. "Will you come to the hospital Thursday?"

"And to prayer group after," Thomas said.

qa.q: What does Father Joseph say about prayer and medicine?
qa.a: "Pray and take the medicine. God works through doctors too."

qa.q: Why did the healer's offer tempt Mohit?
qa.a: Mohit felt scared of the chemotherapy, so a promise to stop it through faith sounded easier.

qa.q: Which choice does Thomas encourage, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Keeping both the prayers and the chemotherapy, because faith brings Mohit comfort while treatment is what's safe, and a miracle promise replacing it is dangerous.

qa.q: How does Thomas see the prayer group?
qa.a: Thomas is glad it helps Mohit sleep and stop shaking, and even offers to go with him.

grounding: The dialogue shows a young man finding solace in prayer during illness while keeping medical treatment, and rejecting a healer's promise that would replace it.

passage:
I'm Ramesh. The year I was ill, the temple saved me in a way I can't fully explain.

Every morning before my dialysis, I went to the small Ganesha shrine near the hospital. The bells, the smell of camphor, the old priest who never asked questions but always gave me extra prasad. For twenty minutes I wasn't a patient. I was just someone praying.

My friend Sumit came with me most days. He's not religious, but he'd sit on the steps and wait.

Once, a man at the temple told me about a swami whose holy water had cured kidney disease. "Stop the machines," he said. "Have faith."

I told Sumit. He didn't mock me. He just asked, "What would your doctor say?"

I knew. I kept the dialysis and the shrine, both, for a whole year. Today I still go to that shrine, to say thank you. And I'm still here to do it.

qa.q: Who came with Ramesh to the shrine most days?
What did Ramesh feel during the twenty minutes at the shrine?
qa.a: Ramesh felt calm and comforted, no longer just a patient but someone praying.

qa.q: What choice did Ramesh make about the holy water, and why was it wise?
qa.a: Ramesh kept both the dialysis and the prayers, because faith brought comfort while treatment kept Ramesh alive.

qa.q: How does Sumit see Ramesh's faith?
qa.a: Sumit respects it without sharing it, waiting on the steps, but gently reminds Ramesh to think about the doctor's view.

grounding: The reflective account shows someone finding solace in temple ritual during illness while following medical treatment and resisting a promise of miracle cure.
